name: Holiday Party at the Worthington Community Center
host: City of Worthington Parks and Recreation
address: 345 E Wilson Bridge Rd, Worthington, OH 43085
paras: The City of Worthington hosts its annual Holiday Party at the Worthington Community Center, 345 E Wilson Bridge Rd, on Friday, December 11, from 6 to 8 PM. The city lists the party as free.
Santa visits with his reindeer, and the evening includes carnival games and festive activities for families.
The party is part of the city's Parks and Recreation special events lineup, and the Community Center phone is (614) 436-2743.
tip: Plan on an evening visit with Santa and his reindeer, and check the city page for any updates before you go.

name: Children's Christmas at the Orange Johnson House
paras: Children in grades 3 to 5 can spend a Saturday evening living an old-fashioned Christmas in Worthington. Sessions run on Saturdays, December 5, 12 and 19, from 4 to 8 PM, and families choose one date.

Children prepare and eat a typical early 1800s meal, hear Christmas stories, tour the house, play period games, make a craft, sing traditional songs and learn about school traditions. Each child also receives a gift from a very famous visitor.
Advance registration is required and the cost is $35 per child. Questions go to committee chair Dianne Hoover at 614-888-2326.
tip: Pick one of the three Saturdays and book ahead, since advance registration is required.

name: Christmas Traditions: An Historic Holiday Tour
when_note: Thursday, December 10, tours starting at 6:30 PM
ages: Guests who can climb stairs and stand
paras: Worthington's historical society runs an evening tour of Christmas history inside a decorated 19th century home on High Street. Tours start at 6:30 PM on Thursday, December 10, and the listing ends at 8 PM.

History interpreters share stories about Christmas celebrations by Worthington's founders in 1803 and through the 1800s and early 1900s, from Christmas stockings and trees to ghost stories and gift giving.
Plan to reserve ahead: the $15 ticket cannot be refunded, and since the home has several staircases, walking up steps and standing for stretches is part of the evening.
tip: Wear comfortable shoes, since the house has several flights of stairs and the tour includes standing.

name: Snowflake Castle at the Westerville Community Center
when_note: Monday, November 30 through Sunday, December 6, with morning and afternoon or evening sessions
paras: Westerville Parks and Recreation brings back Snowflake Castle at its new home, the Westerville Community Center, 350 N Cleveland Ave. The event runs Monday, November 30 through Sunday, December 6.

Children visit Santa's Workshop to build a wooden toy with the elves, then paint it and take it home. Each ticket also includes a photo with Santa and Mrs. Claus, and families can see Santa's sleigh and the trains.

Tickets are $15 per child and sold online only, with a limit of six per household. Up to two adults may come with each ticketed child. A holiday craft area in Multipurpose 5 needs no ticket, and proceeds go to the Westerville Senior Association. Questions go to santa@westerville.org or (614) 901-6560.
tip: Tickets are online only and the city says the event sells out, so check the city page for open sessions.
